extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, agents, and others considering submitting novels to the Booker Prize
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility and judging standards for the Booker Prize: the award is for the best sustained work of fiction in English published in the UK and/or Ireland, and judges evaluate books on literary merit, sustained quality, originality, prose, resonance, contemporary engagement, formal innovation, and moral seriousness. The page also summarizes the prize's process and the International Booker variant for translated fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stated Criterion (eligibility and core definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The best sustained work of fiction written in English by an author of any nationality, and published in the UK and/or Ireland."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines core eligibility and purpose: must be a sustained (whole-book) work of fiction, written in English, and published in the UK and/or Ireland. This is the canonical formulation judges use to decide what the prize is for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary merit
rubrics_metrics.description: "Literary merit — craft and ambition above all"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges prioritise high-quality craftsmanship and artistic ambition; technical skill, depth of writing, and seriousness of literary intent are primary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained quality
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sustained quality — not just brilliant scenes but a whole book that holds"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on the entire novel's consistency and cumulative effect rather than isolated strong passages; the work must maintain standards across its length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: "Originality of vision — fresh perspective, voice, form"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for works that offer a distinctive viewpoint, an original authorial voice, or novel formal choices that set the book apart from others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive prose
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stylistic qualities matter: sentences should demonstrate control, vitality, and a recognizable authorial style; prose that is vivid and well-crafted is rewarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for books that have lasting emotional or intellectual impact and that continue to offer rewards on subsequent readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with the present moment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Engagement with the present moment — many years' winners speak to contemporary anxieties"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that meaningfully speak to current social, political, or cultural concerns are often favoured; topical relevance and urgent thematic engagement can strengthen a book's case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Formal innovation — Booker often rewards experimental structure (e.g., Lincoln in the Bardo, Milkman)"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental or inventive structural/formal approaches are frequently recognised; examples cited on the page show past winners with unconventional forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Moral seriousness — willing to take on difficult subjects with care"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value novels that handle weighty or challenging moral themes thoughtfully and with care, demonstrating ethical depth rather than nihilism or flippancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process and mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: "5 judges read 150+ submitted novels; Longlist (~13) → Shortlist (6) → Winner"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural expectations: a multi-stage selection (longlist, shortlist, winner) determined by a panel of five judges. Judges rotate annually and the chair can influence the tone and priorities of the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Booker structure (translated fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Same structure for translated fiction; judges fiction in English translation, prize split between author and translator."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the International Booker, the rubric is applied to works in English translation; the prize money is shared between author and translator, and translation quality is implicitly part of evaluation since judges read the English translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural influence / critique
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you have a short-list of six Booker Prize books, people read the one that wins…; the Booker can narrow what counts as literary culture." (Hornby critique)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A meta-consideration: selection can shape literary tastes and the cultural definition of 'literary' work. This is a critique of institutional impact rather than an explicit judging metric, but it signals awareness that winners influence the field.
